result.title: CriticalScenes: Scalable Photorealistic Critical-Scenario Generation for Closed-Loop Driving Adaptation
result.summary: Safety-critical interactions are rare in recorded driving data, leaving end-to-end driving planners with limited exposure to evasive behaviour during training. This lack of critical supervision can lead to unsafe behaviour and, in rare instances, collisions. To address this gap, we introduce CriticalScenes, a reconstruction-based framework that transforms ordinary recorded driving scenes into photorealistic safety-critical interactions with corresponding collision-avoidance supervision. Across 53 reconstructed source scenes, 979 of 1,060 attempted interactions yield feasible threat trajectories (92.4\%), while the inserted threat actors remain detectable in more than 95\% of non-occluded observations within 5--35\,m. Experiments with two structurally different end-to-end planners show that the generated supervision improves critical-scenario planning, while closed-loop transfer varies across planner architectures. SparseDrive achieves a 46.5\% relative reduction in collision rate on an independent photorealistic closed-loop benchmark, whereas UniAD shows only a modest closed-loop improvement despite substantial open-loop gains. The results further highlight the importance of closed-loop evaluation, as improvements in open-loop trajectory prediction do not necessarily translate into equivalent safety gains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出重建式框架 CriticalScenes，将普通车载记录场景改造成逼真的安全关键交互并附带避撞监督，在 53 个源场景上生成 979 条可行威胁轨迹，并用两种结构不同的端到端规划器检验开放环与闭环迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 属较远的驾驶场景生成方向，但其「开放环轨迹指标提升未必转化为闭环安全收益、且迁移随架构而异」的结论，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理与训练监督的真实收益评价方式。
